thread:
sam: heads up — p95 for /chat/create in the latency dashboard jumped ~40ms for eu-west this morning. dashboard shows 210ms, raw events p95 ~170ms. anyone else seeing a mismatch? :eyes:
neha: is that the rollout-aggregated p95 or the raw-query? (which dashboard/time window)
sam: rollout-aggregated p95 (dashboard default 15m). I ran a raw query on the eventstore for the same timeframe and got 170.
diego: could be sampling/origin attribution. we recently flipped a small routing change that proxies some traffic via client-proxy for new clients — maybe sample_origin got lost and we're double-counting those samples in rollups.
neha: do we have the sample_origin tag on the rollup keys? if not, TDigest merge could be mixing different sources with different latency distributions.
lia: question: are our rollups respecting sample_weight/sample_count when merging t-digests? if proxy duplicates requests without adjusting weight, percentiles go up.
matt: observability-bot: routing-change: client-proxy A/B enabled at 3412345600 for route /chat/create (10% traffic).
observability-bot: deploy: routing change pushed by matt — metadata: feature=proxy-ab, %traffic=10, affected_routes=[/chat/create]
diego: quick check — from telemetry logs I see entries like `latency_ms=215 sample_origin=client-proxy` but also entries without sample_origin that look like the original ingress. if the rollup key omitted sample_origin, both streams merged.
sam: here's a quick curl to compare origins: `curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/api/rollups?route=/chat/create&window=15m&group_by=sample_origin" | jq '.'`
neha: thanks. can we short-circuit: add a temporary dashboard breakdown that shows p50/p95/p99 per sample_origin (client, client-proxy, internal) — that'll tell us if proxy is heavier tail.
lia: longer term we should: 1) ensure rollup key includes `sample_origin` for routes where routing alters request path; 2) make rollup merging use `sample_count` as weight when merging tdigest centroids; 3) mark historical rollups as derived-from-mixed-origins so folks don't misinterpret.
matt: I can ship a tiny console change — a collapsed toggle in the latency widget: "Break down by sample_origin" (default off). UX OK? @neha?
neha: default off is fine, we don't want a crowded UI. but surface a small warning if rollup keys are missing origin tag for the selected range.
diego: immediate mitigation: when routing change was flipped, we could have emitted an annotation to dashboards — we didn't. add an incident-note? at least annotate the timeline so oncall isn't surprised.
observability-bot: alert-suppression: p95 anomaly suppressed for /chat/create between 3412345600-3412348000 due to known routing change (manual).
sam: plan for action items: (A) add `sample_origin` to rollup key for affected endpoints (diego); (B) patch rollup merge to validate sample_count weighting (lia); (C) small console toggle + tooltip about mixed origins (matt); (D) backfill annotation and add timeline note + update alert doc (neha). I'll open the umbrella ticket and assign.
matt: I can have a console PR ready by EOD with the toggle UI and tooltip text.
diego: i'll start a quick data-check script to compute pctl per origin for the last 48h and post results here.
lia: migration note — backfilling historical tdigest rollups is expensive; we should mark past rollups as "untrusted_for_origin_breakdowns" instead of computing everything.
sam: ok thanks — sounds like we know the root cause (origin-tag missing + weighting). can we run a 24-48h canary after fixes and compare dashboard vs raw p95? route fix to 10% -> 100% and observe.
neha: agreed. please include the raw event p95 in the canary dashboard so we can verify.
sam: i'll create the umbrella ticket now and add the checklist. :thumbsup:
